chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Humeed ibn Ziyad al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn as-Sabah ibn ad-Dhahhak narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a from Sayf at-Tammar from Abu al-Murhaf, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The hasteners will perish.' I asked: 'And who are the hasteners?' He said: 'Those who hurry. And the near ones will be saved, and the fortress stands firm on its pegs. Be the rear guard of your homes, for the dust is upon the one who stirs it, and they will not wish distress upon you except that Allah afflicts them with a distraction, except for whoever encounters them.'

key_terms.أَحْلَاسَ: Rear guard; those who stay behind or guard the rear
key_terms.الْحِصْنُ: The fortress; symbolizing stability and firmness
key_terms.الْغُبْرَةَ: The dust; metaphor for the turmoil or consequences of sedition
key_terms.الْمُحَاضِرُونَ: The hasteners; those who rush into affairs or fitnah
key_terms.الْمُسْتَعْجِلُونَ: The hurried ones; those who impatiently seek deliverance or action
key_terms.الْمُقَرَّبُونَ: The near ones; those close to God through patience

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'al-muhadirun' mean in the context of waiting for the Mahdi?
ai.summary: In the era of the Great Occultation, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies 'al-muhadirun' as those who impatiently seek immediate political deliverance, contrasting them with the 'muqarrabun' who maintain steadfastness. This hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the Shia doctrine of *al-intizar* (waiting), advising believers to remain in their 'homes'—symbolizing spiritual and social stability—to avoid the 'dust' of fitna, as Allah will distract their pursuers unless they actively provoke conflict. The metaphor of the fortress standing on its 'pegs' (awtid) highlights the enduring nature of the true believers' position amidst transient turmoil.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (5) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Hameed bin Ziyad al-Kufi from Ali bin as-Sabah bin ad-Dhahhak from Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Suma’a from Sayf at-Tammar from Abul Murhaf that

Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “The hasteners will perish and those nearest to Allah will be saved! Keep to your homes because seditions will be against those, who cause them! Whenever they wish you a distress, Allah afflicts them with what makes them busy away from you except those, who follow them.”
